author: bd-spin/bd-spin-20260512T045359Z-1929490
text:
Decomposed into 8 child beads per the description's 'Suggested decomposition' section:

- JMAP-cf7p.1 (P3): Scaffold — crate dir, Cargo.toml publish=false, dep wiring (axum, tokio, tokio-tungstenite with rustls-tls, 8 server crates + memory features)
- JMAP-cf7p.2 (P3): Axum router — POST /jmap + GET /.well-known/jmap [depends on .1]
- JMAP-cf7p.3 (P3): Wire 8 reference MemoryBackends [depends on .2]
- JMAP-cf7p.4 (P3): SSE GET /events per RFC 8620 §7.3 [depends on .3]
- JMAP-cf7p.5 (P3): WebSocket GET /ws per RFC 8887 [depends on .3]
- JMAP-cf7p.6 (P3): Bearer auth middleware (constant-time compare via subtle) [depends on .2]
- JMAP-cf7p.7 (P3): spawn_in_process() lib API + smoke test [depends on .3 and .6]
- JMAP-cf7p.8 (P4): README + rustdoc NOT-FOR-PRODUCTION warnings [depends on .7]

Only .1 is currently ready (others blocked by their deps). The autonomous /do-beads loop can now pick up .1 in a future session, then .2/.6 in parallel after .1 closes, etc.

Note for the .1 claimant: workspace TLS-stack policy (per workspace AGENTS.md) requires tokio-tungstenite be declared with default-features=false and only rustls-tls-* features enabled. 'cargo tree -i openssl --workspace' must continue to report 'did not match any packages' after .1 lands.

Note for the .3 claimant: each of the 8 extension server crates' exact register_*_handlers function name needs to be verified before wiring. The bead body lists best-guess names but a few may differ.
